show: 「1457, 소년 잠들다」 — a Korean original musical created and performed by the theatre company 극단 시와 별 (Theatre Poem & Star), staged at 서일대 배양관 예다움홀 in Seoul, 2026
synopsis:
Dan-jong, still scarcely more than a child, is torn from the throne when his uncle Su-yang Daegun seizes royal power. Sent away to Yeongwol, he carries with him the loss of a crown, the uncertainty of survival, and an aching separation from Jeong-sun Wanghu, whose love remains beyond his reach. As the young king faces exile, the human world around him reveals its cruelest forces: ambition that devours kinship, political calculation that abandons loyalty, and fear that turns even devotion into danger.

Three Najdokkaebi watch over the story from the margins of the living and the dead. Mischievous, irreverent, and compassionate by turns, they observe the suffering that humans inflict upon one another, folding the tragedy into the legends of Yeongwol. Their presence gives voice to the landscape itself: a place haunted by grief, yet guarded by spirits unwilling to leave an innocent boy wholly alone. Through them, moments of playfulness and wonder interrupt the encroaching darkness, even as Dan-jong's hopes for peace grow more fragile.

Dan-jong clings to memories of Jeong-sun Wanghu and to the possibility that loyalty and tenderness might outlast violence. Yet the order against him arrives, and he is compelled to accept sayak. His death does not end the tale; it becomes the beginning of a vigil. The Najdokkaebi remain near the boy who has been made to sleep, challenging the living to confront the cost of forgetting him. In remembrance, grief becomes not merely sorrow but an act of shelter for the dead.

The musical meditates on innocence destroyed by power, and on love that persists through exile, death, and distance. It also asks whether compassion and collective memory can offer dignity to those history has wronged.

show: 7080 뮤지컬 목마와 숙녀 (Korean title: 「7080 뮤지컬 〈목마와 숙녀〉 - 부산」) — produced by 북구문화예술회관, staged at 부산북구문화예술회관 in Busan, 2026
synopsis:
A man sits alone in a quiet cafe, drawing music from his guitar while the room around him seems suspended between the present and an earlier age. A woman enters his field of memory, and their tentative exchange opens a path to the loves, separations, and youthful promises that still reverberate beneath familiar melodies. As song after song rises, the cafe becomes a shared inner landscape where recollection is never fixed: laughter returns beside regret, a once-bright romance is recalled through the ache of its ending, and ordinary encounters acquire the weight of moments that could not be held.

The man and woman move through emotional fragments rather than a straightforward chronology. Their voices summon scenes of waiting, confession, companionship, and farewell, tracing how love can remain vivid even after the people involved have gone their separate ways. The distance between them is softened by music, yet each melody also reveals what time has taken away. Memories of youth, loneliness, and an absent beloved mingle with the quiet poetry of a horse’s bell receding into the distance, suggesting a world in which people must continue onward while carrying what they have lost.

The audience is drawn into this intimate journey as a living chorus. Familiar songs invite shared voices, turning private nostalgia into a communal act of remembrance and allowing the characters’ emotional story to expand beyond the cafe.

At its heart, the musical considers how love and memory survive through song, even when relationships, youth, and certainty have passed. It balances the warmth of reunion with the melancholy of parting, finding consolation in the act of remembering together.

show: 창작뮤지컬 BACK TO 1931 : 시무언 이용도 (Korean title: 「창작뮤지컬 〈BACK TO 1931 : 시무언 이용도〉」) — a Korean production, staged at 윤당아트홀 1관 in Seoul, 2026
synopsis:
Jua skips worship as university life fills with exams, credentials, career anxieties, and the pressure to keep pace with everyone around her. Her faith has slipped into the background, despite her mother's persistent concern and prayers. When a parcel arrives containing a book about Pastor Yi Yongdo and some cookies, Jua accepts it with irritation rather than interest. She eats, falls asleep, and awakens far from her familiar world: in Pyeongyang in 1931, inside a church alive with worship and revival.

There Jua encounters Yi Yongdo, the young preacher known as Simeon, whose intense devotion and searching words unsettle her assumptions. As she watches him serve others, embrace poverty and sharing, and call a complacent church toward renewal, Jua is drawn into the fervour and hardship of his ministry. The distance between their eras begins to narrow. Her own worries about achievement, employment, and social expectation are placed beside Yi Yongdo's insistence that a life cannot be measured only by worldly standards.

Jua does not receive an easy solution to her uncertainty. Instead, her meetings with Yi Yongdo force her to confront what she has neglected, why her faith has grown cold, and where she stands when ambition and spiritual conviction pull in opposite directions. The journey through 1931 becomes a personal reckoning, inviting her to return to the present with a changed understanding of purpose, love, prayer, and responsibility.

The musical centres on the conflict between external success and an inward calling. It asks whether faith can be renewed through compassion, humility, and the courage to examine one's own life.

show: Black Mary Poppins (Korean title: 「뮤지컬 〈블랙메리포핀스〉」) — produced by ㈜쇼노트, staged at 링크아트센터 벅스홀 in Seoul, 2026
synopsis:
Hans brings his estranged siblings back together after receiving a notebook connected to the fire that destroyed Dr. Gretzen Schwartz’s mansion twelve years earlier. In 1926, the renowned psychologist had taken in four orphaned children—Hans, Hermann, Anna, and Jonas—who lived under the care of Mary Schmidt, his research assistant and their nanny. When the mansion burned, Dr. Gretzen died and the children survived, rescued by Mary, who was left severely burned. Hailed at first as their saviour, Mary vanished after arson suspicions turned toward her; the traumatised children, unable to remember the night, were separated and adopted into different homes.

Now adults, they return with scars that time has not erased. Hans has become a lawyer but cannot free himself from the past; Hermann channels his instability into painting; Anna has become a teacher whose composure conceals an old terror; and Jonas, working at a publishing house, remains haunted by panic and fractured speech. As they compare memories prompted by the notebook, their recollections clash, overlap, and gradually expose what life in the mansion had concealed. Dr. Gretzen’s experiments had used the children as subjects, repeatedly erasing their memories, particularly after Wednesday sessions that left them unable to account for lost time.

The siblings finally recall the day Anna was chosen for another experiment and the others witnessed her suffering. Jonas, overwhelmed by rage, pushed Dr. Gretzen, causing his death. Hermann then took responsibility for the body and set the fire, while all four children became bound to the act and its aftermath. Mary did not betray them: at their desperate request, she used hypnosis to bury the truth and protect them. Reclaiming those memories twelve years later, Hans, Hermann, Anna, and Jonas must decide whether to seek oblivion again or endure the pain together.

The musical confronts childhood abuse, trauma, guilt, and the unreliable nature of memory. Its central act of healing is not forgetting: it is choosing to acknowledge unbearable truth, mourn what was lost, and continue living with one another.

show: Brahms (Korean title: 「뮤지컬 〈브람스〉」) — produced by KT&G 상상마당 대치아트홀, NTA컴퍼니, PH E&M(주식회사 피에이치이엔엠), staged at KT&G 상상마당 대치아트홀 in Seoul, 2026
synopsis:
Johannes Brahms leaves home in 1853, carrying little more than his talent and a fierce desire to study with the composer he reveres, Robert Alexander Schumann. When he reaches the Schumanns’ household, Robert recognises an exceptional young musician and welcomes him into a world of artistic ambition, intense friendship, and uncompromising ideals. There Brahms hears Clara Schumann play, and her music awakens in him an emotion he cannot easily name: admiration becomes devotion, and devotion becomes a love he believes he has no right to possess.

As Brahms works beside Robert and Clara, the three artists draw inspiration from one another while their private wounds deepen. Robert’s faith in Brahms’s promise gives the younger man confidence, yet Brahms is troubled by the distance between his own aspirations and the greatness expected of him. Clara, a celebrated pianist, bears the pressures of marriage, motherhood, performance, and Robert’s increasingly unstable condition. Brahms tries to suppress his feelings for her, ashamed that his heart has turned toward the wife of the man who has become both mentor and friend.

Robert’s illness worsens into hallucinations and despair, leading him to attempt to take his own life. In the aftermath, Clara struggles with anguish and uncertainty, while Brahms remains at her side, unable to cure her grief yet determined not to abandon her. He turns to composition as the only language capable of holding what cannot be spoken: longing, guilt, loyalty, and love. Observing these lives is the painter Max Klinger, whose perspective frames the artists not merely as celebrated names, but as people driven by the need to leave something truthful behind.

The musical portrays art as both a refuge and a burden: a way to transform suffering without escaping it. It centres on the fragile boundary between love and devotion, and on the cost of pursuing beauty when human relationships cannot be resolved as neatly as music.

show: 'Cafe-in' (Korean title: 「뮤지컬 〈카페인〉」) — produced by ㈜피알컴퍼니, staged at 대학로 더굿씨어터 in Seoul, 2026
synopsis:
Each morning, Sejin unlocks the doors of the cafe Love is..., grinds the coffee beans, and writes a new answer to the words “Love is...” on the chalkboard. She is the cafe’s manager and barista, devoted to the daytime world of espresso, quiet routines, and a romantic ideal she cannot quite put into practice. At six o’clock, the space changes hands: wine replaces coffee, and Jimin, the night-shift sommelier, takes over. Although they never meet, he cannot resist answering Sejin’s earnest chalkboard declarations with teasing objections. Their written exchanges soon become a lively private battle between two people who know each other only through handwriting, wit, and opposing opinions about love.

Curious about the woman behind the board, Jimin visits during the day while pretending to be a customer. Rather than give his real name, he introduces himself as Jeongmin. Sejin, charmed by the considerate coffee lover who seems to understand her, begins to fall for “Jeongmin,” unaware that he is the same irritating sommelier who mocks her messages every evening. Jimin then finds himself caught between two identities: as Jimin, he keeps sparring with Sejin through the chalkboard; as Jeongmin, he offers her warmth, encouragement, and eventually advice on how to pursue the very man he is pretending to be.

What begins as a prank grows increasingly difficult to control. Jimin’s deception brings Sejin closer to him, yet it also builds the misunderstanding that may hurt her most. As their unseen rivalry becomes intimacy and the cafe’s divided hours draw their lives together, both must confront whether affection founded on a lie can become honest love.

The musical treats love as both coffee and wine: bitter, sweet, stimulating, and capable of lingering long after the first taste. Its central themes are the gap between fantasy and truth, the vulnerability beneath flirtation, and the courage required to be known without disguise.

show: Club Seolhwa (Korean title: 「뮤지컬 Club 〈설화〉」) — produced by ㈜73컴퍼니, staged at 극장 온 in Seoul, 2026
synopsis:
The petitions have reached Heaven, and their clamor overflows into Club Seolhwa, where Okhwangsangje convenes an extraordinary public vote: after five thousand years of stories, who has been treated most unfairly? Summoned from the world of old tales into a pulsing contemporary club, the candidates arrive determined to challenge the versions of themselves that audiences think they know.

Horangi steps forward to protest the simplifications that have reduced a formidable being to a stock villain or fool. Dokkaebi energizes the proceedings while presiding over a contest in which wit, presence, and performance matter as much as grievance. Nolbu refuses to accept that he should bear the full burden of an infamous reputation, presenting his own side of the story with shameless conviction. Gumiho, long burdened by fearful portrayals, makes a case for the pain and complexity concealed behind a supernatural image. Around them, Kkachi and Kkamagwi marshal the gathering, guide the rival claimants, and turn the dispute into a night of music, dance, and direct appeal.

Each contestant recounts a personal history of misjudgment, asking the crowd not merely to sympathize but to decide whose complaint deserves to prevail. The prize is extravagant: the winner receives a cathartic salpuri celebration and, more importantly, the chance to have their story rewritten. Yet no fixed verdict can settle the argument. As the competing accounts collide, the audience must weigh charm against remorse, familiar legend against a newly heard testimony, and choose the evening's most wronged figure.

The musical plays with the instability of reputation: a tale repeated for generations can harden into a judgment, while the person inside it loses the right to speak. By making the audience the final arbiter, it asks who gets to tell a story, who benefits from its version of events, and whether a public can ever fairly measure another's hurt.

show: Gwanghwamun Love Song (Korean title: 「뮤지컬 〈광화문연가〉」) — produced by CJ ENM │ 제작대행: 유한회사 커넥트씨, staged at 디큐브 링크아트센터 in Seoul, 2026
synopsis:
Myeong-woo opens his eyes in the Memory Exhibition Hall with only a minute of life remaining. At the threshold of death, he meets Wol-ha, the enigmatic master of memories and keeper of human connections, who offers to lead him back through the moments that have shaped him. As the present-day composer revisits his past, his younger self reappears: a shy art student whose life changes when he encounters Su-a at a spring sketching contest in Deoksugung.

Bright, forthright, and impossible to ignore, Su-a draws the young Myeong-woo into days of friendship and tentative romance. Their shared time in and around Gwanghwamun carries the promise of a first love, yet the political unrest surrounding them soon forces a division between private feeling and public conscience. Myeong-woo witnesses Su-a at a demonstration and sees her beaten and taken away during the violent suppression of the protesters. Unable to protect her, he is left with a guilt that he cannot voice and an increasingly painful distance between them.

Myeong-woo enters military service while Su-a commits herself to the movement, and the path that might have joined them slips away. Guided by Wol-ha through recollections that shift between tenderness, fantasy, and unbearable regret, the older Myeong-woo confronts the rooms and absences within his memory, including the love he never fully understood, his long marriage to Si-yeong, and Su-a’s later life with Jung-gon. The journey compels him to face not only what he lost, but also the choices, fears, and silences that made those losses permanent.

At its heart, the musical considers how love survives in memory even when it cannot survive in life. It is a farewell shaped by first love, remorse, mortality, and the possibility of accepting one’s past before the final moment arrives.

show: HAEMONGGA (Korean title: 「뮤지컬 〈해몽가〉」) — produced by (주)나인스토리, staged at 예스24스테이지 1관 in Seoul, 2026
synopsis:
Yugyeon earns small coins in the Hanyang market by reading strangers' dreams and treating their ailments with acupuncture, until a desperate visitor interrupts his ordinary trade. The visitor is Yi San, the Crown Prince, who has not slept peacefully for years. Tormented every night by the same nightmare, he offers Yugyeon a lavish reward if the dream interpreter can free him from the darkness that closes in whenever he tries to rest.

Lured by the promised payment, Yugyeon enters the palace and becomes Yi San's physician. He attempts to impose order on the prince's disordered days, observing his habits, treating his body, and pressing him to recount the visions he has tried to suppress. Yet Yi San's sleeplessness cannot be explained as a simple illness. Political enemies watch for signs of weakness, threats of assassination surround him, and the pressure of his position leaves him increasingly unstable. Even the royal robe becomes unbearable to wear, while hallucinations and fits of madness make his claim to the throne appear dangerously fragile.

At the center of Yi San's terror stands Sado, his father, whose death Yi San witnessed and whose fate continues to invade the prince's dreams. Yugyeon tries to interpret each recurring image and trace the illness back to its source, believing that naming the nightmare may rob it of its power. But as their sessions draw Yi San further into memories he cannot control, the boundary between dream and waking life begins to dissolve. A concealed truth emerges from beneath the nightmares, bringing danger to both men and changing the uneasy bond between healer and patient. Yi San must confront what he has feared to remember if he is to survive the night and retain his place in the palace.
The musical centers on trauma, grief, insomnia, and the psychological violence of political power. It asks whether painful memories can be escaped, or whether recovery requires facing them directly and choosing to live beyond them.

show: 「모노뮤지컬 His-Story」 — produced by CMP, staged at 플레이더씨어터 in Seoul, 2026
synopsis:
A phone rings just as Jesus cries out from the cross, wrenching the audience away from the familiar image of crucifixion and into the cluttered room of a musical writer. Commissioned by a pastor to create a work about Jesus, the writer struggles to find a form that will not merely repeat a story everyone thinks they already know. He begins to test an idea: Jesus will not speak for himself alone. Instead, the people who encountered him will step forward, each revealing a different face of the man at the centre of their lives.

As the writer imagines and performs the parts, the story moves from prophecy and birth towards judgment and execution. Yosep confronts the mystery of a child whose arrival upends ordinary expectations. Dongbang Baksas proclaim the birth of the Messiah, while a Rabbi debates the twelve-year-old Jesus and is unsettled by the boy's insight. Sebang Yohan recognises the promised figure in Jesus, but the Devil challenges him in the wilderness, pressing him to turn spiritual calling into power and spectacle.

The writer shifts rapidly among witnesses, opponents, followers, and the crowd. Garot Yuda's disillusionment hardens into betrayal. Herod ridicules the prisoner brought before him, and Pilate weighs political expediency against conscience. Barabbas becomes part of the cruel choice made by a crowd that demands release for one prisoner and death for another. Through these conflicting voices, Jesus emerges not as a distant icon but as someone who provokes faith, fear, hope, anger, and misunderstanding. The journey returns at last to Golgotha, where the cross completes the story the writer has been trying to understand.

The musical considers how a life can be known through the testimonies of those who loved, opposed, used, doubted, or abandoned its subject. It centres on belief, betrayal, moral responsibility, and the unsettling force of a figure whose meaning remains contested by every witness.

show: HUNKY SHOW (Korean title: 「뮤지컬 헝키쇼 (HUNKY SHOW)」) — produced by 아라컴퍼니, staged at 스타스테이지 in Seoul, 2025
synopsis:
The doors of Lolo BAR open onto a night of music, mischief, and cocktails, where one Boss presides over five irresistible bartenders and the women in the room are welcomed as far more than spectators. Each bartender arrives under the name of a drink—MAKGEOLLI, MOJITO, GIN, HIGHBALL, JACK DANIEL’S, BALLANTINE’S, CHI-CHI, CHIVAS REGAL, JUNGLE JUICE, KAHLÚA, MARTINI, JOHNNIE WALKER, or TSINGTAO—bringing a distinct style, energy, and charm to the bar’s shifting encounters. The Boss keeps the evening moving, mixing orders, teasing rivalries, and inviting the guests to surrender themselves to the atmosphere.

As the bartenders serve their special cocktails, the apparently ordinary bar becomes a place where every look can become a joke, every dance can turn into a challenge, and every customer can be drawn into the action. Flirtation, comic misunderstandings, bold confessions, and exuberant dance numbers collide as the men compete to win attention and transform the night into a celebration. The bar’s rules are loose: guests are encouraged to cheer, respond, dance, and share in the escalating party, while the performers constantly reshape the mood around the reactions in the room. What begins as a drink after dark develops into an all-out show of charisma, humour, physical performance, and collective release.

By the end, Lolo BAR has offered its guests not simply a cocktail but a temporary escape: a chance to laugh loudly, feel glamorous, and be carried along by a room full of music and unapologetic energy. The Boss and bartenders leave the night suspended in a final toast, turning an evening at the bar into a shared memory.

At its heart, HUNKY SHOW celebrates self-expression, confidence, and the pleasure of being fully present in the moment. Its comic, participatory format turns desire and playful fantasy into communal celebration rather than private spectacle.

show: LET ME FLY (Korean title: 「뮤지컬 〈렛미플라이〉」) — produced by (유)렛미플라이, 엔에이치엔링크㈜, staged at 두산아트센터 연강홀 in Seoul, 2026
synopsis:
Namwon stretches toward the night sky, struggling to tune a radio as Apollo 11 races toward the moon in 1969. A gifted repairman with a long-suppressed dream of becoming a fashion designer, he has just received a letter that seems to bring that impossible future within reach. Beside him is Jeongbun, the young woman he loves, whose own ambition is to explore the moon as an astronaut. As the pair imagine leaving for Seoul and building a brighter tomorrow, the full moon swells unnaturally overhead. Namwon collapses beneath its light.

He wakes in 2020, no longer young but a seventy-year-old man in the same cramped lodging-house room. The future is both unfamiliar and disturbingly intimate: he runs a small alterations shop rather than living the life of fashion he once envisioned, and an elderly woman named Seonhee calls him Halabeom. Namwon cannot understand where the decades have gone, why Jeongbun is absent, or how this quiet life could possibly be his. Determined to return to 1969 before the future hardens around him, he begins an urgent search through the strange world that has become his present.

As Namwon confronts his older self and listens to Seonhee, fragments of the years he cannot remember begin to surface. Past and present overlap through remembered objects, everyday routines, lost aspirations, and the enduring traces of Jeongbun. The more fiercely Namwon tries to reclaim the future he imagined with her, the more he must face the choices, sacrifices, disappointments, and unexpected happiness that formed the life he actually lived. What first appears to be a comic journey through time becomes a reckoning with love, memory, and the meaning of an ordinary life.

At its heart, the musical treats life as a time journey made from small choices rather than perfect achievements. It suggests that dreams may change shape, but love and shared days can give even an imperfect life its lasting radiance.

show: Let the Cheongsachorong Shine! (Korean title: 「창작가무극 〈청사초롱 불 밝혀라〉」) — produced by (재)서울예술단, staged at 국립정동극장 in Seoul, 2026
synopsis:
Yundeok is preparing another immaculate celebration at Cheongsachorong, Joseon's most sought-after marriage house, when Nodeul arrives with an extraordinary commission. He wants a wedding for his widowed mother, who has spent years alone keeping her tavern and raising him. In a society where remarriage is forbidden, the request risks scandal as well as punishment, but Nodeul refuses to accept that his mother's life should end with widowhood. Moved by his determination, Yundeok promises to create a ceremony worthy of her long-silenced hopes.

Yundeok rallies Cheongsachorong's spirited specialists: Imo, an ingenious problem-solver; Icheol, the fashion-conscious master of scissors; Gonji, who fashions a bride's beauty; and singers Yangpyeong and Gapyeong. Together they turn preparations for an illicit second marriage into a daring campaign of costumes, flowers, music, gifts, and carefully managed secrets. As the household works, Nodeul's mother must confront not merely public disapproval but her own fear of choosing joy after years defined by loss and duty.

Their plans become still more precarious when Laurent, a wealthy Qing merchant, takes an interest in Cheongsachorong. He proposes acquiring the business and expanding it beyond Joseon, yet his intentions are distorted through the interpretations of Jinam, the official translator accompanying him. Misunderstandings multiply, mistrust grows, and Jinam devises a scheme that could let Laurent seize Cheongsachorong for himself. With the wedding approaching, Yundeok must defend both the company and the couple's right to stand before their community and receive its blessing. The festivity becomes a test of whether custom will yield to compassion, and whether a ceremony can honor a love society has tried to deny.

At its heart, the musical celebrates the desire to be loved, recognized, and blessed rather than merely to satisfy the institution of marriage. It contrasts restrictive convention and commercial ambition with quiet sincerity, family devotion, and the courage to begin again.

show: M. Butterfly (Korean title: 「뮤지컬 〈엠. 버터플라이〉」) — a Korean production, staged at 예스24스테이지 1관 in Seoul, 2026
synopsis:
René Gallimard sits in a French prison and summons the story that he has spent years reshaping into the romance of his dreams. In 1960s Beijing, the reserved French consular employee sees Song Liling perform the dying heroine of Madama Butterfly and is captivated by Song's poise, beauty, and apparent vulnerability. Song challenges René's ideas about East and West, yet also seems to offer him the adoration and submission he has never believed possible. Their secret meetings draw René out of his timid life and into an intoxicating private world in which he can imagine himself powerful, desired, and indispensable.

As political tensions deepen, René is forced to leave Beijing with his wife, Helga. Distance does not dissolve his attachment to Song. Eight years later, he abandons the security of his former life and chooses Song again, unaware of the calculations beneath their reunion. Song returns to France and steers René toward access to confidential diplomatic material. René, increasingly devoted to the fantasy that Song embodies, passes on information while refusing every doubt that might shatter the identity he has made for himself.

The affair finally becomes a criminal case. Accused of revealing state secrets, René is compelled to confront facts he has evaded: Song has concealed a life, a body, and a political purpose from him. Song's revelation does not merely expose deception; it destroys René's cherished conviction that he was the author, conqueror, and hero of their love. In prison, reality and performance collapse into one another as René clings to the image of his perfect Butterfly even after it can no longer survive.

show: Midnight — the Korean licensed production 「뮤지컬 〈미드나잇 : 앤틀러스〉」 of the British musical MIDNIGHT, book and lyrics by Timothy Knapman, music by Laurence Mark Wythe, based on the play Citizens of Hell by the Azerbaijani writer Elchin; produced in Seoul by ㈜모먼트메이커, first staged in Korea in 2017
synopsis:
Three violent knocks interrupt Man and Woman’s uneasy New Year’s Eve celebration. Outside, people vanish night after night, taken away without explanation; inside their apartment, the couple tries to persuade itself that love, loyalty, and the simple fact of having survived another year can still offer protection. As midnight approaches, the door opens to Visitor, a stranger who claims he needs only to use the telephone. His calm manner and intrusive familiarity quickly turn the visit into an interrogation.

Visitor seems to know the couple more intimately than any stranger should. He probes the fragile bond between Man and Woman, drawing out the humiliations, compromises, suspicions, and betrayals they have kept hidden from one another. Man, determined to shield his frightened wife, attempts to resist and control the encounter; Woman, terrified of abandonment and of what may lie beyond the apartment door, struggles to hold on to her faith in him. Yet every defence becomes another opening for Visitor. The more fiercely they deny their past, the more clearly their separate acts of self-preservation emerge.

What began as a domestic refuge becomes a courtroom without mercy. Visitor exposes the price that both have paid—or made others pay—to remain safe in a world ruled by fear. Finally, he reveals who he is and presents them with an unbearable final choice: survival will demand a sacrifice, and neither love nor innocence can prevent the decision from being made. With midnight imminent, Man and Woman must confront not only Visitor’s power but also the selves they have become.

The musical examines how terror turns ordinary people against their own consciences and against those they love. It asks whether goodness can endure when survival appears to require complicity, betrayal, or the sacrifice of another human being.

show: 「고백」 (official English title: Musical Love Confession) — a Korean original musical produced by 가프공연예술제, staged at 구로창의아트홀 in Seoul, 2026
synopsis:
A performer stands before the audience and begins to confess—not merely a romantic feeling, but a truth that has long been held back. As the words unfold, the stage becomes a shifting space of memory, hesitation, imagination, and direct address, where private emotion is repeatedly tested by the fear of being misunderstood. Each attempt to speak honestly opens another question: whether love can survive silence, whether a person can reveal their heart without losing the safety of concealment, and whether a confession is made for the beloved or for the confessor themself.

The action moves through encounters charged with uncertainty. Ordinary exchanges acquire weight as unspoken affection lingers beneath them, while moments of closeness are interrupted by doubt, timing, and the tendency to retreat just before the decisive words can be said. Characters circle around what they want to tell one another, revisiting memories and possibilities that expose the distance between inner feeling and outward behaviour. Songs give shape to thoughts too fragile or complicated for plain conversation, allowing longing, embarrassment, hope, and regret to coexist rather than resolve immediately.

As the confessions accumulate, no single declaration remains simple. To speak is to risk rejection; to stay quiet is to accept the possibility of permanent loss. The characters must confront the versions of themselves they have performed for others and decide whether sincerity can be an act of courage rather than a final demand for an answer. By bringing concealed feelings into the open, they discover that the outcome of a confession cannot be controlled—but choosing to make it may still change the person who speaks.

The musical centres on the courage required to be emotionally truthful, especially when love offers no guarantee of reciprocity. It considers silence and speech, vulnerability and self-protection, and the possibility that honest connection begins when people stop hiding behind what they cannot say.

show: The Origin of Species (Korean title: 「뮤지컬 〈종의 기원〉」) — produced by ㈜뷰티풀웨이, staged at 동덕여자대학교 공연예술센터 코튼홀 in Seoul, 2026
synopsis:
Yujin wakes to a call from Haejin and steps into a home shattered by violence: his mother, Jiwon, lies brutally murdered. The discovery tears open a life Yujin has tried to keep orderly and forgettable. Once a gifted swimmer, he lost the sport that had been his one refuge after suffering a seizure during the Doha Asian Games national-team trials. His mother and his aunt, Hyewon, a doctor, responded by forbidding him to swim and placing him on a drug called Remote, insisting that his illness and impulses must be controlled.

Now living as a law-school applicant, Yujin has learned to endure the rules imposed on him. He secretly stops taking Remote and slips out at night, seeking a fragile sense of freedom beyond the surveillance of Jiwon and Hyewon. Haejin, a gentle and attentive film student, is Yujin's only close friend. Yet Haejin's place in the family is unsettling: he was taken in because he bears an uncanny resemblance to Yumin, Yujin's dead older brother.

As further suspicious deaths and buried memories emerge, Yujin begins tracing the links among the murder, the medication, his family's strict discipline, and the past that everyone around him has concealed. Every answer destabilizes his sense of himself. The investigation becomes inseparable from a more frightening question: whether the darkness pressing in on him comes from the people who have controlled his life, or from a violent nature within him that has been waiting to surface. In confronting the truth about Jiwon, Hyewon, Haejin, and Yumin, Yujin must decide what he is willing to acknowledge—and what he will become.

The musical examines the collision between control and instinct, asking whether cruelty is inherited, awakened, or created through fear and confinement. It also turns family into a site of both protection and manipulation, where self-knowledge arrives through terror rather than comfort.

show: Park Yeol (Korean title: 「뮤지컬 〈박열〉」) — produced by ㈜더블케이엔터테인먼트, staged at 링크아트센터드림 드림4관 in Seoul, 2026
synopsis:
Rumours race through the shattered streets of Tokyo after the Great Kanto Earthquake of 1923: Koreans are said to be plotting violence amid the chaos. As the lie feeds panic and enables the massacre of Korean residents, public scrutiny begins to threaten the authorities. Ryuji, head of the Tokyo Prosecutors' Office, receives a blunt order: find a sensational case powerful enough to divert attention from the killings.

His search turns to Park Yeol, a Korean anarchist committed to resisting imperial power, and Kaneko Fumiko, his Japanese wife and comrade. The authorities seize on fragments of an alleged bomb plot, intending to inflate them into an exemplary prosecution. Arrested and interrogated, Park Yeol and Fumiko quickly understand that they have been selected as convenient villains in a state-made spectacle. Rather than merely deny the accusation, they decide to seize control of the role imposed upon them.

Before the court, the pair proclaim that they intended to assassinate the Crown Prince and demand the death penalty, transforming Ryuji's carefully engineered case into a public confrontation with the Japanese state. Their defiance turns the trial into a platform for their anarchist conviction that no person should rule over another, and that Koreans and Japanese alike deserve freedom and dignity. Yet the authorities fear that executions would make the two into martyrs. The sentences are commuted, and Park Yeol and Fumiko are separated in prison. Fumiko dies in captivity; years later, following Korea's liberation, Park Yeol is released, carrying the memory of their shared struggle.

The musical centres on resistance to state violence, the manipulation of truth, and the courage to turn persecution into testimony. It also portrays love and solidarity across nationality as a force that endures even when power tries to isolate, silence, and erase its opponents.

show: Romeo & Juliet (Korean title: 「R＆J - 양평」) — a Korean production, staged at 이함캠퍼스 in Gyeonggi Province, 2026
synopsis:
A street brawl erupts between two households whose old hostility has poisoned the town, and Romeo, a young man caught in the restless heat of the conflict, longs for a love that can give his life another direction. At a masked gathering held by the rival family, he sees Juliet. Their recognition is immediate: amid music, movement, and danger, the two young people discover a fierce intimacy that seems to make every inherited division irrelevant. Only after they have pledged themselves to one another do they learn that their families stand on opposite sides of the feud.

Romeo and Juliet refuse to let that revelation separate them. With the help of Friar Laurence, they marry in secret, hoping their union may turn private devotion into a bridge between enemies. Instead, the violence surrounding them closes in. Tybalt provokes Romeo, Mercutio is killed, and Romeo answers grief with revenge. His punishment is banishment, leaving Juliet trapped between her new marriage and the demands of a family that expects her to accept another future.

Desperate to escape, Juliet accepts Friar Laurence's dangerous plan: she will drink a potion that makes her appear dead, then awaken and flee with Romeo. But the message explaining the scheme fails to reach him. Romeo arrives at the tomb believing Juliet has truly died, chooses death beside her, and drinks poison. Juliet wakes moments later, finds him dead, and takes her own life. Their bodies finally force the feuding families to confront the human cost of their hatred.

The musical centres on love struggling to survive within a world ruled by inherited resentment, masculine pride, and uncontrolled violence. Its tragedy lies in the contrast between two young people who imagine a shared future and the social forces that deny them time to live it.

show: SOCRATES PARADOX (Korean title: 「뮤지컬 〈소크라테스 패러독스〉」) — produced by HJ컬쳐㈜, staged at NOL 서경스퀘어 스콘 1관 in Seoul, 2026
synopsis:
Socrates steps before the Athenian court as Meletos, a young poet, accuses him of rejecting the city’s gods and corrupting its youth. The charge gives public shape to years of resentment. Ever since the oracle at the temple of Delphoi declared that no one was wiser than Socrates, he has searched among politicians, poets, craftsmen, and supposed experts for the meaning of that pronouncement. Each encounter has led him to the same discovery: people who claim certainty often cannot defend what they say they know. Socrates concludes that his only wisdom lies in recognising the limits of his own knowledge.

Carrying that conviction into the streets of Athina, he questions strangers, exposes contradictions in accepted beliefs, and challenges the ambition, vanity, and complacency of those with influence. To some young people, his relentless questioning opens a path toward independent thought. To others, especially the powerful citizens unsettled by his influence, he becomes an intolerable provocation. Meletos is brought forward as the voice of this opposition, insisting that Socrates has endangered the city by leading its young away from tradition and reverence.

Before a jury of five hundred, Socrates conducts his own defence. He tests Meletos’s allegations point by point, forcing his accuser to confront the inconsistencies in his case. Rather than plead for pity or flatter the court, Socrates argues that his questioning is a duty entrusted to him, a necessary sting against a society too willing to mistake reputation for truth. His defence may reveal the weakness of the accusations, but it cannot overcome the hostility gathered against him.

The court finds Socrates guilty and places him under the shadow of death. Even then, he refuses to bargain away his principles or beg to be spared. Facing the sentence with unwavering composure, he chooses fidelity to truth over a life purchased through silence.

The musical centres on the paradox that genuine wisdom begins with knowing one’s ignorance. It pits individual conscience against public fear, asking whether a society can endure the voice that refuses easy answers.

show: Someday (Korean title: 「뮤지컬 〈썸데이〉 - 용인」) — produced by (재)용인문화재단, 사회적협동조합 무하, staged at 용인시 평생학습관 큰어울마당 in Yongin, 2026
synopsis:
Yeonsu sits in the bar Someday, staring at the future she fears she may have to abandon. Although she has earned a place in a highly competitive practical-music programme, her father, Iam, insists that music cannot provide a secure life. Raised by Iam alone and unable to understand his harsh opposition, Yeonsu feels that the dream she has fought for is slipping away before it can begin. At Someday, the bar owner Yeonhui offers her a mysterious diary, and an unexpected drink sends her into the past.

Yeonsu awakens in 1994, at the time when Iam himself is twenty. There she finds not the stern father she knows, but a young man passionately pursuing music and singing with his friends. She also meets Jihae, a young woman of Yeonsu's own age whose warmth and familiarity draw Yeonsu close. As they become friends, Yeonsu gradually realizes that Jihae is the mother she barely remembers and that the hopeful young musician before her is her father.

At first, Yeonsu believes that helping young Iam preserve his musical ambitions will change the future and free her to sing. Yet the more time she spends beside Iam, Jihae, and Yeonhui, the more she learns about the choices that shaped her family. Iam and Jihae's love deepens, but their happiness is shadowed by Jihae's illness and the painful decisions demanded by the life growing within her. Yeonsu watches the parents she once misunderstood face loss, devotion, and sacrifice, and begins to see why Iam became afraid of the very dream he once loved.

Someday is ultimately about meeting one's parents not as fixed parental figures, but as vulnerable young people with dreams, grief, and impossible choices. Through Yeonsu's journey across time, it connects the courage to pursue music with forgiveness, family love, and the wish to understand the past before choosing one's own future.

show: Turbulent age (Korean title: 「뮤지컬 〈난세〉 : 정도전과 이방원의 이야기」) — produced by ㈜콘텐츠플래닝, staged at NOL 서경스퀘어 스콘 2관 in Seoul, 2026
synopsis:
Across a janggi board on the eve of the First Strife of Princes, Jeong Dojeon and Yi Bangwon sit face to face, their conversation sharpened by the knowledge that neither may survive the coming night. Once bound by trust, they revisit the years in which they stood together amid the collapse of Goryeo, convinced that a ruined age demanded a new political order. Jeong Dojeon, the brilliant scholar and architect of revolution, sees in Yi Seonggye the force capable of overthrowing the old dynasty and founding a country governed through institutions, learned ministers, and a vision of rule for the people. Yi Bangwon, Yi Seonggye's fifth son, becomes Jeong Dojeon's devoted ally and pupil, lending resolve and action to the shared cause.

Their alliance helps bring a new dynasty into being, but victory exposes divisions that revolution had concealed. Jeong Dojeon seeks to curb royal power and secure the succession around a new heir, believing that a stable state must not depend upon the ambitions of a single ruler. Yi Bangwon, passed over in the distribution of honours and excluded from the succession he believes he has earned, comes to regard Jeong Dojeon's plans as both an insult and a threat to his family's future. The mentor who once offered him a path becomes the obstacle he cannot allow to remain.

As Yi Seonggye falls ill, the fragile balance inside the new court collapses. Jeong Dojeon tries to protect the political order he has designed, while Yi Bangwon gathers the will to strike first. Their recollections of shared ideals turn into accusations: each claims to be saving the nation, yet each sees the other's survival as fatal. The night advances toward bloodshed, forcing both men to confront what their revolution has made of them.

The musical examines how companionship can fracture when ideals meet power. It asks whether a nation can truly be built for its people when those who invoke the people are also fighting to determine who will rule.

show: Welcome to the Hyunam-Dong Bookshop (Korean title: 「뮤지컬 〈어서 오세요, 휴남동 서점입니다〉 - 서울」) — a Korean production, staged at 루미나아트홀 in Seoul, 2025
synopsis:
Yeongju unlocks the door of a small, quiet bookshop in Hyunam-dong after leaving behind the exhaustion and pressure that once ruled her life. At first, she has little purpose beyond opening the shop each morning and closing it each night, but she gradually turns the space into a place where people may linger rather than simply buy books. When she hires Minjun, a young man worn down by repeated attempts to find work, the bookshop gains the warm scent and steady rhythm of a cafe. Minjun has abandoned the race to prove himself through employment, yet serving coffee and listening to visitors slowly teach him that a life need not be exceptional to be worthwhile.

People with private burdens begin to gather there. Jeongseo, hurt by unstable work and unfair treatment, seeks calm through knitting and meditation. Huiju worries over her disengaged teenage son, Mincheol, whose lack of ambition and joy makes both mother and son feel trapped. Asked to visit the shop regularly, Mincheol initially arrives without enthusiasm, but the conversations, books, and unhurried company of Hyunam-dong Bookshop give him room to voice questions he cannot easily ask elsewhere. Sangsu becomes a dependable presence among the regulars, while Jimi, who supplies coffee beans, brings her own troubled domestic life into the circle. Seungwoo, a sharp-tongued writer, enters Yeongju's world as a new connection whose candour challenges her guardedness.

As coffee is poured, books are recommended, and ordinary worries are spoken aloud, the visitors do not find easy solutions. Instead, they learn to pause, hear one another, and take modest but meaningful steps toward lives they can accept as their own.

The musical centers on recovery from burnout, loneliness, and the pressure to measure life by conventional success. It celebrates the quiet power of books, patient listening, chosen community, and the courage to begin again at one's own pace.

show: WIDERSTAND (Korean title: 「뮤지컬 〈비더슈탄트〉」) — produced by (주)라이브러리컴퍼니, (주)미스틱컬처, staged at 링크아트센터드림 드림1관 in Seoul, 2026
synopsis:
Magnus grips his foil with a single-minded dream: to become Germany’s finest fencer. In 1938, when ordinary training halls are abruptly shut down, he and his closest friend, Abel Luther, enter the prestigious Eid Sports School, the only place where they can continue to train. There they meet the formidable senior Frederick Karl and fellow students Hagen Axmann and Jasper Muller, but the school’s promise of athletic excellence quickly gives way to a brutal regimen of obedience, hierarchy, racial doctrine, and military discipline. Questions are forbidden; personal feeling is treated as weakness.

When Abel and Jasper resist, they are confined in an underground room, where they uncover a forbidden radio and a coded message left by Rainer, a gifted former fencing student whose death was dismissed as an accident. Following Rainer’s clues, the boys find documents revealing Eid’s true purpose: it is a disguised elite military academy, grooming students for compulsory service while isolating them from the outside world. Abel, Jasper, Hagen, and Magnus begin to circulate the evidence and broadcast the truth, calling their covert movement Widerstand.

Yet Magnus is drawn toward another path. Reinhardt Clare, the school’s director and a celebrated fencer whom Magnus admires, singles him out for special instruction and offers him status, victory, and power. As Magnus rises within the school, Clare orders him to identify the rebels. His fear of helplessness and hunger for recognition estrange him from Abel, just as the group’s resistance becomes more dangerous. Abel’s death forces Magnus to confront what silence, ambition, and obedience have cost. Carrying Abel’s final plea to protect him, Magnus enters a national fencing final that may bring him within reach of Hitler himself, and chooses to turn the weapon meant to win glory into an instrument of defiance.

Widerstand examines the moral price of ambition under authoritarian power, asking whether personal achievement can ever justify complicity. It is also a story of friendship, memory, love, and the resolve to protect others even when resistance demands everything.

show: WTOF Million Loves (Korean title: 「WTOF 〈Million Loves〉」) — produced by 국립중앙극장 (National Theater of Korea) — 2026-2027 국립극장 레퍼토리시즌, staged at 달오름극장(국립중앙극장) in Seoul, 2026
synopsis:
A succession of familiar Korean popular songs opens doors onto changing moments in romance: first attractions, nervous confessions, exhilarating courtship, quarrels, breakups, longing, and the memories that remain after love has passed. Across a broad sweep of time, different lovers encounter the same hopes and disappointments in new forms, turning private feelings into scenes that reflect the shifting texture of everyday life in Korea.

The action traces not one isolated couple but a shared emotional history. Young people test the courage required to speak honestly; partners enjoy the heady certainty of being chosen, then discover how quickly affection can be strained by misunderstanding, circumstance, and time. Some relationships end before they can fully begin, while others survive through compromise and renewed recognition. Songs associated with particular eras supply the language that characters cannot always find for themselves, connecting personal milestones to the collective memories carried by popular music.

As each episode gives way to another, declarations of love, comic misunderstandings, heartbreak, and reunion accumulate into a portrait of romance as people experience it repeatedly across their lives. The music evokes the period in which each feeling was first heard, while allowing audiences to recognize that desire, regret, jealousy, devotion, and consolation recur regardless of generation. The result is a journey through Korea's history of love, shaped through 42 hit songs rather than a single linear romance.

The musical considers love as both intensely individual and widely shared: a source of joy, vulnerability, loss, and endurance. It also celebrates popular song as a living archive, preserving the emotional atmosphere of successive generations while bringing their experiences into conversation.

show: Your Letter (Korean title: 「뮤지컬 〈연의 편지〉」) — produced by (주)수컴퍼니, staged at 플러스씨어터 in Seoul, 2026
synopsis:
Sori opens the desk drawer in her unfamiliar classroom and finds an unsigned letter waiting inside. Having transferred to Cheongsan High after trying to defend a classmate from bullying at her former school, she carries the hurt of becoming isolated herself. The new school feels no safer: every corridor is strange, every new face difficult to trust, and the memory of what happened makes even ordinary days feel exhausting. Yet the letter speaks with unexpected kindness. It offers a shortcut through the school, observations about teachers and students, and a clue leading to another message.

Intrigued, Sori follows the trail. Each letter directs her to a different corner of the campus and turns the school into a quiet treasure hunt. The unknown writer seems to understand exactly how frightening it is to arrive somewhere new, gently urging Sori to look closer, take another step, and believe that connection may still be possible. While seeking the next clue, she repeatedly encounters Park Dongsun, a classmate whose blunt, prickly manner conceals a considerate nature. Their reluctant encounters become companionship, and Dongsun joins Sori in searching for the letters.

As the pair gathers all ten messages, Sori begins to know the people and places around her rather than seeing them only through the distance created by fear. The hunt draws her toward Jeong Hoyeon, the elusive figure associated with the letters, whose presence gives the mystery an almost dreamlike pull. At the same time, the respectable-looking class president An Seunggyu reveals a more rebellious and unsettling side, complicating the fragile relationships forming around Sori. Following the anonymous voice to its end, Sori confronts the lingering wounds of her past and recognizes the sincere care that has been waiting for her in the present.

At its heart, the musical is about the courage to reopen oneself after cruelty and loneliness. Its letters transform a school into a space of memory, friendship, and recovery, suggesting that small acts of kindness can guide someone back toward trust.

show: 가족뮤지컬 사랑해져라 (Korean title: 「가족뮤지컬 사랑해져라 - 대구」) — produced by 봉 컴퍼니, staged at 대덕문화전당 드림홀 in Daegu, 2026
synopsis:
Inside an old wardrobe, a child discovers a secret passage and watches in alarm as Appa disappears beyond it. Refusing to be left behind, the child steps through the hidden doorway and enters a fantastical realm where the ordinary rules of home no longer apply. The search for Appa becomes a lively journey across the border between reality and imagination, filled with encounters that test the child's courage, curiosity, and willingness to trust unfamiliar friends.

As the child follows the trail left by the missing parent, strange figures, animated objects, and larger-than-life puppet companions turn each new obstacle into an adventure. Some offer guidance, while others create confusion or danger; all of them force the child to look beyond first impressions. The world behind the wardrobe is colourful and unpredictable, but its wonders are shadowed by the fear that Appa may remain lost forever. Songs and playful theatrical episodes carry the child from one challenge to the next, transforming moments of loneliness and worry into chances to act bravely.

The journey gradually reveals that finding Appa requires more than simply retracing his steps. The child must face uncertainty, make choices independently, and recognise the love that connects a family even when its members are separated. Moving between the fantastic world and the familiar one, the child learns that courage can grow from longing, and that home is strengthened by the effort to return to one another.

At its heart, the show celebrates a child's imagination as a source of resilience in the face of fear and separation. It also centres on family love, trust, and the courage to seek connection when someone precious seems out of reach.

show: 그날들 (Korean title: 「뮤지컬 〈그날들〉 - 이천」) — produced by 이천시 이천문화재단, staged at 이천아트홀 대공연장 in Icheon, 2026
synopsis:
Jeonghak receives an urgent report during a commemorative event at Cheong Wa Dae: Hana, the President's daughter, has vanished together with her assigned guard, Daesik. Now head of security, Jeonghak recognizes an alarming pattern in their disappearance, one that leads him back to 1992 and the unresolved day that reshaped his life.

Twenty years earlier, Jeonghak entered Cheong Wa Dae as an exemplary but rigid young guard. There he met Muyoung, a gifted fellow recruit whose easy wit and free-spirited manner clashed with Jeonghak's discipline. Competition gradually becomes friendship as the two prove themselves among the strongest of their class. On the eve of a major diplomatic occasion, they receive their first sensitive assignment: protect Geunyeo, a woman whose identity is concealed even from the guards charged with watching her. Confined and isolated, Geunyeo longs for a life beyond the walls around her. As Jeonghak and Muyoung come to know her, their duty becomes entangled with affection, pity, suspicion, and an increasingly dangerous awareness that powerful people may want her silenced.

Then Geunyeo disappears. Muyoung disappears with her, and Jeonghak is left behind to bear the consequences of an event no official account will fully explain. In 2012, Hana and Daesik's flight revives the old mystery. Jeonghak follows a trail through places, objects, and memories that connect the missing pair to Muyoung and Geunyeo. As the past and present mirror one another, the investigation forces him to confront what he believed about loyalty, abandonment, and the choices made in the name of protection. The search for Hana and Daesik becomes a chance to uncover the truth buried for two decades.

The musical centers on friendship tested by duty, love constrained by power, and the lasting cost of secrets. Its parallel disappearances suggest that memory cannot be contained indefinitely: unless the past is faced honestly, its unfinished choices echo into another generation.

show: 김종욱 찾기 (Korean title: 「뮤지컬 〈김종욱 찾기〉」) — produced by CJ ENM / 주식회사 네오, staged at 대학로 틴틴홀 in Seoul, 2026
synopsis:
After losing his job and his girlfriend in quick succession, Geu Namja hears a stranger speak wistfully of finding a first love and turns the idea into a business. He opens Cheotsarang Chatgi Jusik Hoesa, a tiny agency devoted to locating the people clients have never quite forgotten. His first customer is Geu Yeoja, who arrives under pressure from her father to settle down and marry, yet remains unable to let go of the man she met years earlier while travelling in India: Gim Jonguk.

Her information is almost useless. She knows only his name, remembers a brief journey and a promise to meet again in Seoul, and carries the idealised memory of a young man who seemed to embody the future she wanted. Nevertheless, Geu Namja approaches the assignment with dogged professionalism. He tracks down one Gim Jonguk after another, arranging interviews that lead to comic disappointments, awkward misunderstandings, and increasingly improbable possibilities. Geu Yeoja repeatedly finds reasons that each candidate cannot be the one she remembers, suggesting that the search is less about identification than about protecting a cherished past from reality.

As the investigation takes them through encounters with many people and places, Geu Namja and Geu Yeoja spend more time together. His practical persistence clashes with her romantic hesitation, but their bickering becomes companionship. Geu Namja gradually recognises that his feelings for her have moved beyond client and investigator; Geu Yeoja, meanwhile, must confront why she has held onto Gim Jonguk for so long and whether she truly wishes to find him. When evidence finally brings the elusive first love within reach, the outcome forces her to distinguish memory from love and to choose how she will live in the present.

The musical considers first love as both a private dream and a refuge from adult uncertainty. It celebrates the courage to face unfinished feelings, while suggesting that genuine connection may appear not in an idealised past but in the person who shares the difficult search.

show: 나의 첫사랑 레시피 (Korean title: 「나의 첫사랑 레시피 - 대전」) — a Korean production, staged at 이수아트홀 in Daejeon, 2026
synopsis:
Sion faces his thirtieth birthday alone, still carrying the memory of Yesul, the first love he never managed to forget. A lifelong single man accustomed to eating by himself, he discovers an impossible rule: whenever he takes a bite of truly delicious food, he is thrown back into the past. The taste on his tongue becomes a door to the moments that shaped him, and Sion seizes the chance to return to the time when Yesul was still within reach.

At first, the journeys seem like the answer to every regret. Sion can revisit old encounters, speak words he once swallowed, and try to understand the food preferences and small habits that separated him from Yesul. Each new dish offers another opportunity to alter a decision, improve an impression, or turn a missed moment into the beginning of the romance he wanted. His pursuit unfolds amid spirited arguments over food tastes and the pleasures of eating, as everyday choices take on unexpectedly high stakes.

Yet the past refuses to behave like a simple recipe. Changes made in one visit reshape the present in ways Sion cannot predict, and each attempt to get closer to Yesul complicates his life further. The more urgently he tries to construct the perfect version of their relationship, the more he must confront the difference between loving a real person and clinging to an idealized memory. Food, once a companion to his solitude, becomes both the mechanism of escape and a reminder that happiness cannot be recovered merely by repeating the past.

As Sion moves between longing, comic misadventure, and painful recognition, he must decide whether to keep rewriting yesterday or accept the life and emotions before him. His search for Yesul gradually becomes a search for the courage to face his own loneliness honestly.

The musical treats first love as something sweet, lingering, and impossible to reproduce exactly. Through time travel and shared food, it considers regret, personal growth, and the choice to value genuine connection over a perfected fantasy.

show: 「놐놐놐」 — a Korean production, staged at 후암스테이지 in Seoul, 2026
synopsis:
Kim, an elderly collector of waste paper, discovers on a rain-lashed summer night that the stack he has painstakingly saved has vanished from the shabby apartment building known as Paper House. The loss turns the residents against one another. Each tenant carries private disappointments, old wounds, and habits of keeping a door firmly shut, so suspicion spreads faster than sympathy. Before long, their attention fixes on the girl in Room 204, a young recluse whom no one truly knows and whom the neighbours have already learned to regard as strange.

As accusations harden, an unexpected paper aeroplane changes the course of the quarrel. Written across it in uneven handwriting is the confession the girl has never been able to voice directly: her loneliness, the reasons behind her isolation, and the truth of what happened to Kim's paper. The message forces the residents to confront not only their mistaken certainty about Room 204, but also the ways they have abandoned one another while living side by side. What began as a dispute over discarded paper becomes a hesitant search for connection, as people separated by age, experience, and hurt begin to listen. The paper aeroplane passes between closed rooms like an invitation, making visible the fragile possibility that something cast aside can be received, remade, and given value again.

The musical centres on renewal: of waste paper, damaged trust, and people who feel unwanted. It argues that coexistence begins when suspicion gives way to attention, and when a community chooses to circulate care rather than discard those who need it.

show: 「늦은 봄날」 — a Korean production, staged at 대학로 블랙박스 1357 in Seoul, 2026
synopsis:
Mingyeong throws herself into rehearsals with the fierce determination of a newcomer who has waited too long for her first real chance onstage. Yet enthusiasm cannot conceal how unready she feels: the role she longs to play remains beyond her reach, and each setback leaves her more exhausted, embarrassed, and convinced that nothing in her life is moving forward. On a rare day off, she is pushed into returning to the hometown she has avoided for twenty years.

The village appears almost untouched by time. Familiar paths, old houses, and the rhythms of its residents draw Mingyeong into a place she had thought belonged only to childhood memory. Instead of finding the quiet escape she expects, she is caught up in a succession of mishaps involving the village's Postman ajjeossi and the people around him. Their intrusions are comic, insistent, and increasingly difficult to dismiss. Through small encounters, unexpected deliveries, and conversations that stir feelings she has buried, Mingyeong begins to reconnect with the part of herself that had once trusted easily in people and in the future.

Her return also brings her face to face with memories of first love. What initially seems like nostalgia becomes something more complicated: a confrontation with the hopes she carried away from the village, the disappointments that made her abandon them, and the tenderness she has tried to outgrow. As the present continually collides with the past, Mingyeong learns that moving on does not require erasing what came before. The people of the village help her recognize that the dreams she considered lost may still be waiting for her to claim them in a different form.

The musical centers on recovery, first love, and the healing power of returning to a place where one was once known. It suggests that even after disappointment and delay, affection, memory, and courage can make a late spring possible.

show: 달콤한 위로 초코파이 (Korean title: 「뮤지컬 〈달콤한 위로 초코파이〉」) — produced by (사)소리문화창작소 신, staged at 성수아트홀 in Seoul, 2026
synopsis:
Inside Dong-o Bakery on Paldal-ro in mid-1980s Jeonju, the scent of fresh bread masks the tension between its aging owner, Aboji, and his grown son, Dong-o. Twenty-five years earlier, a fire left Dong-o scarred and Aboji haunted by guilt, and the unspoken memory has hardened their relationship into a routine of sharp words, stubborn silence, and work that neither man can abandon. When Dong-o realizes that Aboji is showing early signs of dementia, he decides to take responsibility for the bakery before time and illness take it away from them.

Aboji resists. Still ruled by the terror of the old accident, he sees Dong-o's wish to inherit the shop not as devotion but as another danger waiting to happen. Dong-o, hurt by his father's distrust yet determined to earn recognition, throws himself into creating a new specialty: a sweet Choco Pie. He experiments with the pastry as the people around the bakery bring their own warmth, memories, friendships, and youthful hopes into its crowded kitchen. The new confection becomes more than a business idea; it is Dong-o's attempt to speak to Aboji in the language they both understand--the patient labor of baking and the comfort of something made by hand.

But Dong-o's urgency and ambition drive him too far. A second fire erupts, echoing the disaster that divided father and son decades before and forcing them to confront the grief, fear, and resentment each has carried alone. Amid the shock of loss and the fragility of memory, the bakery becomes the place where their damaged bond can finally be named, tested, and slowly repaired.

The musical treats a Choco Pie as a small but powerful token of care: something sweet offered when words are difficult, pain is old, and reconciliation feels impossible. It centers on familial love, intergenerational healing, memory, forgiveness, and the sustaining warmth of a neighborhood gathered around a shared table.

show: 「런던레코드」 — a Korean production, staged at 엠스테이지 1관 in Seoul, 2026
synopsis:
John opens another quiet morning by sorting dusty albums in his old record shop on the outskirts of London. Once the charismatic leader of a band that seemed to flash across the world and vanish like a comet, he now keeps his past carefully buried beneath the shop’s shelves, routines, and fading music. Few customers come through the door, and the records that once promised escape have become reminders of the dream he abandoned.

Charlie arrives carrying a large suitcase crowded with odd treasures collected after travelling around the world. Restless, curious, and eager to turn every encounter into a story, he brings a burst of movement into John’s stagnant life. Before John can regain his usual composure, Scarlett enters as well, discouraged after failing an audition. She has come to the shop with the heavy certainty that her ambition has reached a dead end, yet the music surrounding her makes it impossible to ignore the part of herself that still wants to sing.

The three strangers initially seem to have little in common. John has learned to protect himself from disappointment, Charlie lives through new experiences without settling anywhere, and Scarlett fears that one rejection has proved she is not meant for the stage. But as they share songs, memories, and the private failures they have tried to conceal, the shop becomes more than a neglected place of business. John’s former identity as the leader of a legendary vanished band gradually emerges, challenging him to face the life he left behind.

Encouraged by one another, John, Charlie, and Scarlett reshape their chance meeting into a creative partnership. Their music gives each of them a way to acknowledge old wounds, reclaim confidence, and risk pursuing a future that had seemed closed.

The musical centres on dreams postponed by fear, failure, and loneliness. It celebrates music as a force that connects strangers, heals disappointment, and makes renewed courage possible.

show: 만천명월 격쟁을 허하라 (Korean title: 「뮤지컬〈만천명월 격쟁을 허하라〉 - 화성」) — produced by 화성특례시, staged at 화성예술의전당 동탄아트홀 in Hwaseong, 2026
synopsis:
The royal procession gathers at Changdeokgung as Jeongjo prepares to travel with his mother, Hyegyeonggung Hongssi, toward Hyeollyungwon in Hwaseong, where his father Sado is buried. Carrying the burden of Sado's violent death and the danger that has shadowed his own life, Jeongjo turns the journey into more than a filial pilgrimage: he orders a new road, the construction of Siheung Haenggung, and an official progress through the towns that lie between the capital and his father's tomb.

At Siheung Haenggung, the pageantry of the royal route gives way to the pressing reality of ordinary lives. Men and women who cannot rely on formal written petitions step into the king's path, strike gongs and small percussion instruments, and risk punishment to make their grievances heard. Their act is gyeokjaeng: a direct public appeal to the sovereign. Among officials, the sudden voices of the crowd create alarm. Some fear disorder, insist on protocol, and regard the petitioners as an interruption to royal dignity. Jeongjo, however, refuses to let ceremony silence suffering.

As each appeal breaks through the guards and officials, the king confronts the distance between a ruler's ideals and the hardships endured by the people. He listens to those dismissed because of their status, poverty, or inability to write, insisting that even the humblest subject remains part of the nation he is bound to protect. His exchanges with the petitioners test his resolve, while the memories of Sado sharpen his awareness of how power can wound when it ceases to hear those beneath it. By the time the procession turns homeward, Siheung Haenggung has become a place where royal authority is measured not by spectacle, but by the willingness to receive a painful truth.

The musical centres on compassionate rule, civic courage, and the human necessity of being heard. It presents gyeokjaeng as both a plea for justice and a living bond between Jeongjo and the people whose voices give moral meaning to his reign.

show: 말하지 못한 사랑 (Korean title: 「말하지 못한 사랑 - 대전」) — a Korean production, staged at 대전 상상아트홀 in Daejeon, 2026
synopsis:
Seoyeon steps back into an old rehearsal room, where the air still seems to hold the voices of the friends she once loved and left behind. Carrying wounds she has never fully named, she is startled when Dongju brings her together again with Jihun and Yuna. Years have passed since the four shared their dreams, their jokes, and the fragile closeness of youth, yet the reunion immediately exposes everything time has failed to settle. Each of them has learned to conceal pain in a different way: Seoyeon has guarded her heart behind composure; Jihun has allowed silence to stand in for the feelings he could not bring himself to voice; Dongju disguises loneliness with humor and easy warmth; and Yuna, afraid of what intimacy might demand, has repeatedly fled just as a relationship begins to matter.

At first, the reunion is awkward, punctuated by teasing memories and careful conversational detours. Dongju tries to restore the easy bond they once had, but the others cannot keep avoiding the past. Old misunderstandings surface, along with resentment over absences, broken promises, and words that should have been spoken long ago. Most painfully, Seoyeon and Jihun must confront the distance created not by a lack of feeling, but by their shared reluctance to risk rejection. As memories return, the rehearsal room becomes a place where the four friends replay the moments that divided them and discover how much of their hurt arose from assumptions left unchallenged.

Their conversations gradually turn into confessions. No apology can erase the years they lost, but admitting fear, regret, and affection makes a different future possible. By facing the love they once left unspoken, Seoyeon, Jihun, Dongju, and Yuna begin to choose honesty over escape.

The musical centers on the cost of silence and the courage required to reveal one's true feelings. It suggests that love can remain alive beneath resentment and distance, but only communication can give it a chance to heal.

show: 「키사를 찾아서」 — a Korean original children's musical, season 8 of the 무대는 내 친구 series, produced by 군포문화예술회관, staged at its 수리홀 in Gunpo, 2026
synopsis:
After the last audience members have gone home, a small cat named Kisa slips into the quiet theatre and begins an adventure that turns the empty building into a world of secrets. Beyond the stage and its sleeping lights lies the wider landscape beneath Surisan, where two children live near the Azalea Garden. When they unexpectedly encounter Kisa, curiosity quickly grows into friendship. The cat is not merely a stray passing through their day: Kisa has been driven away from the neighbourhood and needs somewhere safe to belong.

The children refuse to abandon their new friend. Together, they set out to help Kisa, moving through a nature-filled world in which each discovery asks them to look more carefully at the lives around them. Their journey is shaped by songs, play, and moments of participation, as the children learn what it means to listen to an animal that cannot speak in their words. What begins as a chance meeting becomes a shared mission: to protect Kisa from loneliness and exclusion, and to find a way for the cat to live safely alongside the people of the community.

As their search unfolds, the children confront the fear and indifference that caused Kisa to be cast out. Rather than answering those attitudes with force, they rely on patience, affection, and the courage to stand beside someone vulnerable. The theatre itself becomes part of the magic, suggesting that after people leave and the official performance ends, other lives and other stories continue in the shadows. By helping Kisa, the children discover that care is an action, not just a feeling, and that a small act of welcome can change the world of another living being.

The musical centres on empathy, respect for life, and coexistence between people and animals. It suggests that love, mutual care, and the willingness to make room for others are stronger than rejection or fear.

show: 물속의 달 - 오필리어 (Korean title: 「물속의 달 - 오필리어 (대전)」) — a Korean production, staged at 대전 상상아트홀 in Daejeon, 2026
synopsis:
A gunshot shatters the palace air, and Ophelia stands at its centre: beautiful, unsteady, and armed. From this violent moment, the story moves backward through the events that have driven her toward ruin. Her love for Hamlet, once the source of her most urgent hopes, becomes entangled with the secrets and rivalries of the court. Summoned by Claudius together with her father Polonius, Ophelia is tempted with a radiant vision of the future: marriage to Hamlet and a place of security beside him. The offer has a price. Claudius asks her to watch Hamlet closely and report what she learns.

Caught between a father who expects obedience, a king who exploits her trust, and a lover whose behaviour grows unpredictable and cruel, Ophelia begins a hidden double life. She listens, observes, and relays what she knows, while trying to preserve the love she believes she shares with Hamlet. Yet each act of surveillance turns affection into suspicion. Hamlet’s grief and apparent madness wound her; his distance, sudden rage, and painful words leave her struggling to distinguish truth from performance. Ophelia refuses simply to endure in silence. She pleads for love, fights to hold onto Hamlet, confronts him in anger, and searches for the truth behind the forces tearing them apart.

When Hamlet kills Polonius, Ophelia loses both her father and the fragile balance that has sustained her. Her grief deepens into isolation as the court closes around her, and the path leading to the opening gunshot and to her death becomes unmistakable. Her story is not merely one of helpless collapse, but of a woman trying to act, choose, and understand within a world that continually turns her feelings into instruments of power.

The musical centres on love poisoned by surveillance, political ambition, betrayal, and vengeance. It asks whether genuine devotion can survive a system built on manipulation, while reclaiming Ophelia as a figure of desire, anger, resilience, and tragic agency.

show: 「미디어아트 뮤지컬 파랑새」 (Media Art Musical The Blue Bird) — a Korean media-art musical adaptation of Maurice Maeterlinck's play L'Oiseau bleu, staged at 용인시 평생학습관 큰어울마당 in Yongin, 2026
synopsis:
On a cold Christmas Eve, the siblings Tiltil and Mitil are awakened by a mysterious visitor who begs them to find the Blue Bird of Happiness for her sick child. With a magical diamond that reveals the souls hidden inside ordinary things, they set out beyond their poor home, joined by the loyal Dog and Cat, as well as the animated spirits of Light, Fire, Bread, Water, Milk, and Sugar.

Their search leads them through shifting worlds where dazzling images transform the stage around them. In the Land of Memory, Tiltil and Mitil meet beloved grandparents and relatives who seem lost to time, discovering that those remembered with love are never entirely gone. They enter the Palace of Night, where Cat hopes to frighten the children into abandoning their quest; yet Tiltil faces darkness, illness, war, and other hidden terrors without surrendering. In the Forest, the trees accuse humankind of cruelty, while Dog defends the children with unwavering devotion.

The travelers then visit a graveyard, where what appears frightening yields to a vision of renewed life, and they encounter the future children who wait to be born, each carrying an invention, dream, or purpose into the world. Everywhere they look, blue birds appear, but each vanishes, changes color, or proves unable to bring the happiness they seek. At last, exhausted and wiser, Tiltil and Mitil return home.

There they notice that the blue bird they had overlooked all along has been living close beside them. When they offer it to the sick neighbor child, they learn that happiness grows through kindness, sharing, memory, courage, and the ability to recognize the preciousness of everyday life.

The musical presents happiness not as a distant treasure but as something that can be discovered in one’s own home and relationships. Its journey through fear, loss, memory, and hope suggests that love makes the ordinary world luminous.
