show: 바람으로의 여행 (Korean title: 「뮤지컬 바람으로의 여행」) — produced by 엘피스토리, staged at 대학로 스튜디오 블루 in Seoul, 2026
synopsis:
Yi Pungse steps into the audition room at Seoin University determined to become a singer like Kim Gwangseok. Accepted into the campus band Baram, the 1994 freshman joins aspiring radio music producer Choi Goeun and politically engaged Han Gyeore alongside older students Kim Sangbaek, Baek Eunyeong, and Hong Yeonghu, whose ambition is to make music his life. As the six friends rehearse, perform, and prepare to enter the university song festival, affection grows between them and the band becomes the place where their individual hopes find a shared voice.

On the eve of the festival, Yeonghu loses his mother. The devastated group withdraws from the competition, and Pungse leaves for military service. When he returns, the campus has changed. Gyeore has become the cultural director of Hanchongryeon and asks Pungse to sing once at a student demonstration. Pungse agrees, only to be arrested by the police; amid a violent protest, Gyeore dies under circumstances that remain painfully unclear. Eunyeong's father, a senior figure in the Agency for National Security Planning, offers Pungse's release on the condition that she leave to study abroad. With its members separated by grief, coercion, and silence, Baram falls apart.

Twenty years later, Sangbaek and Eunyeong are married and exhausted by the ordinary battles of raising children, while Goeun returns from overseas. Younger students propose a twentieth-anniversary concert for Baram, bringing the surviving friends back to their old songs and unresolved memories. They begin the performance while holding space for the absent Gyeore and for Pungse, who has long vanished from their lives, letting music carry what words and time have failed to repair.

The musical is about youth tested by history, and about how friendship can be both broken and preserved by memory. It treats music as a refuge for longing, loss, love, and the difficult possibility of forgiveness.

show: 「벚꽃동산, 하얀 집」 — a Korean production, staged at 예술마을 그리다 in Gyeonggi Province, 2026
synopsis:
Lopakhin waits in the nursery as dawn breaks, while Dunyasha listens for the carriage bringing Lyubov Andreyevna Ranevskaya home. After years away, Lyubov returns to the white house with her daughter Anya and her attendant Yasha, finding the familiar rooms crowded with servants, relations, old memories, and the burden of debts she has avoided. Her brother Gaev greets the house as though its walls could preserve the family’s vanished prosperity, while Varya, the adopted daughter who has managed the estate, has already learned how little money remains.

The cherry orchard and house are due to be auctioned unless the family can act. Lopakhin, once the son of a serf on the estate and now a successful merchant, proposes a practical rescue: cut down the orchard, divide the land into holiday plots, and rent them out. To Lyubov and Gaev, the plan feels like an assault on childhood, ancestry, and beauty; they postpone decisions, cling to small rituals, and spend what they do not have. Around them, Anya is drawn toward the idealistic student Trofimov, Varya waits in vain for a future with Lopakhin, and the household senses that its old order is ending.

On the day of the auction, music and dancing fill the house as if celebration can hold disaster outside the door. Lopakhin returns with the news that he himself has bought the estate. His victory is inseparable from old humiliation and new power, while Lyubov and Gaev confront the loss they could neither prevent nor fully acknowledge. The family disperses, the white house is emptied, and the sound of axes begins beyond the windows as the orchard is marked for destruction.

The musical turns a private homecoming into a reckoning with time, debt, memory, and social change. Its central sorrow lies in the conflict between preserving a beloved past and surviving the demands of the present.

show: 베어만 : 마지막잎새 (Korean title: 「뮤지컬 베어만 : 마지막잎새」) — a Korean production, staged at 소극장 쇠내골 in Cheongju, 2024
synopsis:
Su and Jonsi arrive in Greenwich Village carrying the same ambition: to paint a masterpiece and make a life as artists. Their excitement is short-lived when pneumonia begins spreading through the city and Jonsi falls gravely ill. Confined indoors, she grows convinced that recovery is beyond her reach. From her window, she fixes her attention on an ivy vine climbing the wall outside and declares that her own life will end when its final leaf drops.

Su refuses to accept her friend’s surrender. She stays near Jonsi, speaks to her with warmth and resolve, and tries to turn her gaze away from the dwindling leaves and back toward the future they once imagined together. Their neighbour, the struggling painter Beoman, also becomes deeply concerned. Though he is an unknown artist who has not yet created the great work he dreams of, he cannot ignore Jonsi’s despair.

As a violent storm approaches, Su fears that the wind and rain will strip away the last leaf, confirming Jonsi’s terrible belief. Beoman, however, finds a way to answer her hopelessness. In the darkness and bad weather, he acts so that, when morning comes, one leaf still appears to remain on the wall. Jonsi sees it holding fast despite the storm. Its endurance unsettles her certainty that death is inevitable and gradually awakens her will to live. As she regains strength, she begins to understand that the leaf was not merely an object outside her window, but a gift made possible by another person’s compassion and courage.

The musical portrays hope as something people can offer one another when fear makes survival seem impossible. It also honours friendship, artistic devotion, and selfless sacrifice, suggesting that even a small sign of endurance can restore someone’s desire to live.

show: 빌의구둣방 (Korean title: 「뮤지컬 빌의구둣방」) — a Korean production, staged at 소극장 쇠내골 in Cheongju, 2021
synopsis:
Bill bends over a pair of hand-sewn shoes in the small workshop his family has kept through generations, trying to preserve the craft that has defined his life. But late-nineteenth-century Europe is changing around him: industrial production makes ready-made goods cheap and fashionable, customers disappear, and the rent goes unpaid. With eviction looming, Bill must choose between abandoning shoemaking for a more secure livelihood and holding on to the work into which he has poured his pride, skill, and years.

His wife, Anne Kret, watches him struggle with both worry and compassion. Bill feels guilty that his devotion to the shop has left her carrying the burden of their precarious life, yet he cannot easily imagine himself becoming someone else. The pressure of hunger, debt, and an unforgiving market turns each day into a test of what dignity costs.

Gilberta arrives at the shop with a conspicuously painful gait. Though she possesses real ability, she has been denied fair treatment and even the chance to work because she limps. Shut out by a society that judges bodies before character and usefulness before humanity, she has learned how quickly hardship can make a person invisible. Seeking help, she comes to Bill's shop and meets Anne Kret.

The encounter brings together people wounded in different ways by the same world. Bill confronts the possibility that his threatened trade still has meaning when it serves another person's needs rather than merely competing for sales. Gilberta, meanwhile, finds a place where her pain is seen rather than dismissed. As their lives cross, the shop becomes more than a failing business: it becomes a space in which empathy, labor, and human connection can challenge the cruelty surrounding them.

The musical considers the human cost of industrial change, economic exclusion, and prejudice against disability. It ultimately asks whether people can recognize their own hardship in someone else's suffering and choose solidarity over indifference.

show: 빨래 (Korean title: 「뮤지컬 〈빨래〉 - 하남」) — produced by (주)하늘이엔티, staged at 하남문화예술회관 대극장(검단홀) in Hanam, 2026
synopsis:
A gust of wind carries Nayoung's laundry across a rooftop in a modest Seoul hillside neighborhood, bringing her face to face with Solongo, the Mongolian young man living nearby. The two begin with an awkward greeting: Nayoung, who has left Gangwon behind and now works at Jeil Bookstore, is wary of this unfamiliar neighbor, while Solongo approaches her with open warmth. Yet the escaped washing becomes a small bridge between them, and repeated encounters on the rooftops and narrow streets gradually reveal the loneliness beneath their everyday routines.

Nayoung came to Seoul hoping to become a writer, but five difficult years have pushed that dream aside. She works long hours at the bookstore, where the pompous owner Ppang mistreats and harasses employees while demanding their obedience. Solongo has spent five years in Korea working at a factory, trying to sustain himself and his family despite precarious employment and unpaid wages. Around them, the tenants of the neighborhood carry their own burdens, sharing gossip, meals, irritation, and occasional care in the cramped dwellings beneath the sky.

When Ppang unfairly dismisses Nayoung's colleague, Nayoung refuses to stay silent. Her protest turns against her, leaving her transferred, marginalized, and threatened with losing her job. At the same time, Solongo cannot pay his rent because his wages have been delayed, placing his home in jeopardy. One night, an exhausted Nayoung drinks alone; Solongo finds her in an alley and walks her home. When drunken men provoke her, he intervenes and is beaten. Their separate humiliations finally become shared knowledge.

Back on the rooftop, Nayoung and Solongo hang washing together and allow tenderness to replace the guardedness of their first meeting. The clothes fluttering between the buildings become a visible sign that grief, anger, and exhaustion can be aired rather than hidden.

The musical centers on people made vulnerable by insecure work, migration, discrimination, and urban isolation. It finds resilience not in an easy escape from hardship, but in small acts of solidarity, dignity, and love.

show: 사랑을 노래하다 (Korean title: 「사랑을 노래하다 - 창원」) — produced by 창원문화재단, staged at 3.15아트홀 대극장 in Changwon, 2026
synopsis:
Miseuk carries a private dream of becoming a singer through the corridors of Machang Middle School in 1984, when the excitement and uncertainty of adolescence shape every ordinary school day. Her desire to stand before an audience and be heard is more than a passing ambition: it offers her a way to imagine a future beyond the limits of her present life. Among classmates, songs, small misunderstandings, and the restless energy of youth, she continues to protect that hope.

Gyeongho notices Miseuk at first sight. Drawn to her bright presence and the seriousness with which she pursues music, he finds himself swept into the unfamiliar world of a first crush. He wants to be close to her, yet his feelings are difficult to say aloud. His attempts to approach her are colored by shyness, awkward gestures, and the fear that a careless word could disturb the fragile friendship beginning between them. As the students share their days, the distance between what they feel and what they can confess becomes the heart of their story.

Music gives voice to the emotions that the characters cannot always express directly. Familiar songs accompany moments of anticipation, embarrassment, longing, and encouragement, turning schoolyard memories into vivid scenes of youthful possibility. Miseuk must decide how firmly she will pursue her dream, while Gyeongho must learn whether affection means holding on to someone or giving them the courage to move toward their own future. Their tentative connection develops amid the warmth, comic confusion, and bittersweet uncertainty of their classmates' lives.

The story celebrates first love as a feeling both tender and brave: easily shaken, but capable of changing how young people see themselves. It also honors music, friendship, and the courage to let a cherished dream be heard.

show: 생텍쥐페리 (Korean title: 「뮤지컬 생텍쥐페리 - 인천」) — produced by 계양구시설관리공단 계양문화회관, staged at 계양문화회관 대공연장 in Incheon, 2026
synopsis:
Twelve-year-old Antoine de Saint-Exupery climbs trees and dreams of fastening wings to a cart so that he can rise into the sky. After an accident, he encounters the Little Prince, a mysterious companion who becomes the keeper of his imagination and his lifelong soul mate. Their friendship gives shape to Antoine's yearning for flight, urging him to look beyond the ordinary world and toward a life in the air.

Years later, Antoine becomes a pilot. At twenty-seven, he is assigned as an airmail pilot at a southern airfield in Morocco, where danger, solitude, and vast distances test the freedom he once imagined as a child. Guillaume, both mentor and friend, recognizes Antoine's restless spirit and gives him a map unlike any other: a singular guide for a journey through uncertain skies. With it, Antoine begins the free flight he has wanted for so long.

Yet the air routes do not merely offer escape. Antoine must confront the distance between the life he dreams of and the people who give that life meaning. Consuelo, likened to a beautiful rose, enters his world with both vulnerability and force. Guillaume remains a steadfast companion, while Leon Werth represents the genuine adulthood Antoine searches for rather than fears. The Little Prince continues to accompany Antoine inwardly, drawing him back to the questions he carried from childhood: what is worth protecting, whom can one truly understand, and how can a person remain open-hearted amid loss and uncertainty.

As Antoine travels between earth and sky, memory, friendship, love, and imagination become interwoven. His flights lead not only across physical landscapes but also toward a clearer understanding of the relationships that make a life irreplaceable.

The musical centers on the pursuit of freedom and the cost of pursuing it. It suggests that growing up does not require abandoning wonder: love, friendship, responsibility, and the ability to see what cannot be measured give flight its deepest purpose.

show: 쇼뮤지컬 드림하이 (Korean title: 「쇼뮤지컬 〈드림하이〉 - 공주」) — produced by 공주문화관광재단, staged at 공주문예회관 대공연장 in Gongju, 2026
synopsis:
Song Samdong steps onto the stage as The K, a global superstar poised for the defining performance of his career. At the very summit of fame, however, a sudden bout of tinnitus shakes his certainty: the music that has carried him from an isolated village to international acclaim may be slipping beyond his reach. Unable to silence memories of his youth, Samdong returns to Kirin Arts High School, the place where he first learned to turn longing, fear, rivalry, and raw ability into song.

The school he finds is no longer the refuge it once was. Principal Si Beomsu and Cha Doyun pursue their own ambitions, placing Kirin Arts High School and its students' future in danger. Samdong's homecoming brings him back into contact with the people who shared his earliest struggles: Jinguk, now confronting a decisive crossroad at the height of his own career; Jason, who has chosen love with Pilsuk over conventional success; and Yun Baekhui, who carries the weight of teaching while hoping her students will avoid the disappointments that scarred her generation. Kang Ohyeok, whose belief in young performers never wavers, remains determined to defend the school and the possibility it represents.

As old friends reunite, unresolved feelings and former competitions return with them. Samdong must confront not only the threat to the school but also his exhausted relationship with his own dream. The friends discover that the ambitions which once separated them can become the source of their solidarity. Through music, dance, and the memories of the stages they shared, they fight to keep Kirin Arts High School alive and to reclaim the courage that first brought them together.

At its heart, the story celebrates dreams as something that can change shape without disappearing. It asks whether success has meaning without the people who helped create it, and finds renewal in friendship, love, mentorship, and the decision to begin again.

show: 오셀로와 이아고 (Korean title: 「뮤지컬 〈오셀로와 이아고〉」) — a Korean production, staged at 대학로 자유극장 in Seoul, 2026
synopsis:
Othello stands before judgment as the victorious general’s past collapses into accusation, memory, and the unbearable question of why he killed Desdemona. Beside him, Iago reconstructs the same catastrophe as a defense of his own ambition: passed over for advancement and determined to seize power, he claims that the world rewards only those willing to manipulate it. Their final statements pull the audience back through the events that joined their fates.

Fresh from military triumph, Othello receives authority in Cyprus, yet the honor cannot silence the insecurity he carries as an outsider of humble origins. His marriage to Desdemona becomes both his greatest solace and the point at which Iago can wound him most deeply. Iago begins arranging insinuations rather than evidence, exploiting Othello’s trust in him while turning ordinary gestures into apparent proof of betrayal. A lost handkerchief, the presence of Cassio, and Iago’s carefully measured hints gradually persuade Othello that Desdemona has given her love to another man.

As suspicion hardens into jealousy, Othello demands certainty but refuses the innocence that stands before him. Desdemona cannot understand the charge against her, and Iago repeatedly adjusts his story to keep Othello trapped inside a vision of dishonor. The general who once commanded armies loses command of himself. In the end, he murders Desdemona in the belief that he is punishing betrayal, only for Iago’s deception to be exposed too late. Othello must confront the irreversible cost of accepting a lie as truth, while Iago faces the consequences of treating human lives as instruments of advancement.

The musical places jealousy, ambition, trust, and manipulation under scrutiny, asking how a person can be driven to destroy what they most love. By allowing Othello and Iago to argue their own cases before the audience, it also examines responsibility: whether ruin belongs only to the schemer, to the deceived man, or to everyone who watched the truth be distorted.

show: 「음악극 소요유」 — produced by (주) 콘텐츠컬쳐플레이스 엘피스토리., staged at 대학로 스카이씨어터 2관 in Seoul, 2026
synopsis:
Dongju steps into a small Daehangno theatre and announces that tonight is Soyoyoo's final concert--and, more unusually, his funeral while he is still alive. The leader and vocalist of the three-piece indie band has received a terminal diagnosis for a progressive brain tumour. As his body, memory, and language threaten to close down, he refuses to let illness dictate a bleak ending. Instead, he gathers the people who have mattered most--family, friends, and fans--so that gratitude can be spoken, heard, and shared before it is too late.

Alongside him are Haru, Soyoyoo's composer and Dongju's longtime lover and musical partner, and Noah, the gifted multi-instrumentalist whose quiet steadiness has made the band a refuge. Together, the three musicians perform the songs from Sanchaek, their first and last new album. Each live number carries traces of their awkward but radiant youth, the years in which love and companionship were forged through music, and the ordinary moments that gradually became precious. Haru shapes their history into melody while Noah sustains the performance with an array of instruments, helping turn the stage into both a concert hall and an intimate farewell.

As the evening deepens, Dongju looks directly at the guests before him and discloses why he arranged this gathering. He also reveals the private meaning concealed within Sanchaek: the album is not simply a final artistic statement, but a way of leaving warmth, laughter, and remembrance with those he loves. The concert becomes an act of parting that resists mourning as its only language. Rather than asking everyone to wait for his absence, Dongju invites them to encounter him fully in the present--singing, remembering, and receiving affection.

show: 이머시브 뮤지컬 좀비 (Korean title: 「이머시브 뮤지컬 〈좀비〉」) — produced by 하모니컴퍼니, 극단서곡, 남극장, staged at 남극장 in Seoul, 2026
synopsis:
Hunter pushes through a city overrun by the infected after the government forms the zombie-eradication committee Z.E.I. to contain the accelerating outbreak. Tasked with securing a vaccine reportedly held in a hospital, this nominally elite agent crosses streets and buildings now claimed by the undead, facing danger with far less competence and certainty than the official mission demands. At the hospital, Hunter encounters Suji, a high-school girl whose infection has transformed her into the body and appearance of an adult man. Suji's family, however, refuse to abandon her. They do not see a monster to be eliminated, but the daughter they know remains somewhere within the frightening new exterior.

The search for a cure becomes entangled with the family's determination to keep Suji alive and Hunter's growing exposure to the human cost hidden behind the language of extermination. As the infected multiply and public fear turns people into categories of threat and contamination, the group must decide whether survival means obeying the logic of eradication or protecting a loved one who no longer looks recognisably human. Hunter's journey through the ruined city gradually becomes a confrontation with his own assumptions about heroism, duty, and who deserves to be saved.

The musical uses a zombie outbreak to examine prejudice, fear, and the ease with which society excludes people who appear different. Its emotional centre is a family's refusal to relinquish love, asking whether humanity lies in a person's outward form or in the bonds that persist despite it.

show: 인사이드 미 (Korean title: 「인사이드 미 (대전)」) — a Korean production, staged at 이수아트홀 in Daejeon, 2026
synopsis:
A spotlight catches IS Inbyeol as she accepts the Influencer of the Year award, smiling flawlessly for the cameras and the followers who know her only through the polished life she posts online. Away from the screen, however, she is Lee Bokja, a woman whose ordinary circumstances and private uncertainties bear little resemblance to the glamorous persona she works tirelessly to sustain. Raised by her grandmother in rural Haenam, Bokja has learned to treat appearance, approval, and rising follower counts as proof that she has become someone worthy of attention.

Her boyfriend, the gentle young composer Choi Jinhyeok, initially supports her ambitions without hesitation. He is given a major opportunity to write a new song for superstar Shanti, yet the success that should bring the couple closer instead exposes the distance between them. Jinhyeok, who has little taste for social media, watches Inbyeol become increasingly consumed by the demands of maintaining IS Inbyeol: every moment must be marketable, every encounter turned into content, and every feeling adjusted for an imagined audience. Encounters with an array of people - including Shanti, a cafe owner, an online-shopping host, Amazon Crew dancers, Bokja's friend Sun-deok, a yoga master, and Bokja's grandmother - keep reflecting different versions of the self that Bokja is trying to conceal.

As the pressure to look happy overwhelms the ability to be happy, the relationship with Jinhyeok fractures. Forced to confront the gap between her public image and the person behind it, Bokja begins to recognize desires, memories, and hurts that no number of likes can erase. Through separation, self-examination, and a renewed encounter with Jinhyeok, she and he begin to seek the unperformed selves they had both lost sight of.

The musical examines the conflict between digital validation and authentic identity. It argues that intimacy and self-worth cannot be built on a carefully curated image, but must begin with accepting the person beneath it.

show: 제물포문화재단 창작뮤지컬 켈로 (Korean title: 「제물포문화재단 창작뮤지컬 〈켈로〉 - 인천」) — produced by (재)제물포문화재단, staged at 제물포구 문화회관 in Incheon, 2026
synopsis:
A group of young women, each carrying a private wound and a reason to survive, volunteer for a mission that offers neither safety nor recognition. In 1950, as the Korean War throws Incheon into chaos, they are gathered under the command of James, a former CIA intelligence officer attached to the US military. Stripped of their ordinary identities, they are trained as clandestine operatives for KLO, the secret unit assigned to gather the intelligence needed for the Incheon Landing Operation. They know one another not by their real names but by code names: Rabbit.

The training is merciless. The women learn to conceal fear, observe enemy movements, deliver intelligence, and trust people they scarcely knew only days before. Their different backgrounds initially keep them apart, yet hardship turns the unit into a fragile chosen family. Each mission tests the boundary between courage and desperation: a message may determine the course of an assault, a moment of hesitation may cost a life, and every return from enemy territory leaves the survivors carrying the absence of those who do not come back.

As preparations for the landing intensify, the women enter an ever more dangerous world of surveillance, deception, divided loyalties, and sudden loss. Their work helps secure the information required for the operation, but their role remains hidden behind the victories claimed by official forces. When the fighting ends, no rank, formal status, or public honour protects them from being erased. The women who risked everything for the operation must confront the bitter reality that history may remember the triumph while forgetting the people who made it possible.

The musical centres on courage that goes unrecorded, and on the cost of being denied a name in history. It also celebrates solidarity: in a war that reduces people to tools and casualties, the women preserve one another through loyalty, memory, and friendship.

show: 조선셰프 한상궁 전주비빔밥 그 맛의 완성 (Korean title: 「조선셰프 한상궁 전주비빔밥 그 맛의 완성 - 전주」) — produced by 전북특별자치도, 전주시, staged at 전주대사습청 야외공연장 in Jeonju, 2026
synopsis:
Han Sanggung escapes the upheaval that follows the Eulmi Incident and leaves the royal kitchen behind, arriving in Jeonju with the skills of a court chef but little sense of where she now belongs. In Nammunjang, she encounters Namsangin, a cloth merchant whose affection and faith in her offer a first welcome, and she is drawn into the noisy life of the market. There, the ingredients that sustain the region step forward as living companions: Ssali, Mugi, Jangi, Muri, Nari, and Kong. Each carries a distinct character and contribution, yet none can make a complete dish alone.

As Hansanggung learns from the people of Jeonju and from the ingredients themselves, she begins to understand that cooking is not merely a display of refinement learned in the palace. It is an act rooted in land, labor, generosity, and the relationships that bring separate elements into harmony. Her growing confidence is tested when Choesanggung emerges as a rival, sharpening the conflict around authority, taste, and the right to define what food should be. At the same time, forces threatening Nammunjang turn the market's future into a matter of survival.

When a World Food Competition is proposed, the merchants place their hopes in Hansanggung and ask her to represent Nammunjang. Faced with rivalry, uncertainty, and the responsibility of protecting the market's dignity, she chooses to stand with its people. Drawing together Jeonju's ingredients, its culinary knowledge, and the community that has accepted her, Hansanggung prepares a bowl of Jeonju bibimbap that embodies more than technical mastery. The contest becomes a chance to defend Jeonju's name and affirm the market's future.

The musical celebrates food as a shared language of memory, place, and human connection. Its idea of completion lies in harmony: among ingredients, among people, and between inherited tradition and a living present.

show: 창작 뮤지컬 늦봄의 길 (Korean title: 「창작 뮤지컬〈늦봄의 길〉 - 안성」) — a Korean production, staged at 안성맞춤아트홀 대공연장 in Anseong, 2026
synopsis:
Music pounds through a crowded gogo club in the spring of 1973, where Juho works amid a young crowd determined to dance away the unease of the times. Drawn there by her friend Jiyoung, Luda catches Juho's eye, and their sudden attraction grows into a tender romance shaped by friendship, ambition, and the fragile exhilaration of youth. Around them, students quietly prepare to resist an increasingly oppressive political order; Juho, once absorbed in his ordinary life, finds himself helping friends whose private anxieties are becoming public risks.

Elsewhere, Mun Ikhwan devotes himself to translating the Bible, seeking meaning in words and faith. Yet the violence and injustice of the country intrude upon that work: the death of his longtime friend Junha, along with other devastating events, makes silence impossible. As the young people confront surveillance, questioning, and fear, Mun Ikhwan resolves to place conscience before safety and joins those preparing the Declaration for National Salvation and Democracy.

The separate paths of the lovers, their activist friends, and Mun Ikhwan converge in 1976 at Myeongdong Cathedral. When the declaration is read aloud, the authorities respond with arrests and imprisonment. Park Yonggil refuses to let the imprisoned be erased from public life. With the wives of other detainees, including Gong Deokgwi, Yi Huiho, and Peimun, she wears a purple shawl and steps into the streets, transforming grief, devotion, and shared danger into an act of defiance. Behind prison walls and beyond them, those who once sought only love, work, or peace must decide what they are willing to sacrifice for a freer future.

The musical traces how individual awakenings become collective courage. It places love, faith, friendship, mourning, and moral responsibility beside the sustained struggle for democracy and human dignity.

show: 충분한 이별 (Korean title: 「뮤지컬 충분한 이별」) — a Korean production, staged at 나온씨어터 in Seoul, 2026
synopsis:
At EXIT, a breakup-agency worker prepares to guide clients through the words they cannot bring themselves to say. People arrive carrying relationships that have already cracked but have not quite ended: some fear the pain of being left, some cannot bear the guilt of leaving, and others cling to familiar affection even after trust, hope, or conversation has run out. The agency promises neither a painless solution nor a convenient erasure. Instead, it becomes a temporary room in which those who have delayed goodbye must face the feelings they have hidden from the people closest to them.

As consultations unfold, clients rehearse confessions, accusations, apologies, and final messages. A farewell that first seems like a practical service proves impossible to reduce to a script: every relationship contains uneven memories, unspoken expectations, and a different measure of what has been given and what remains owed. The workers of EXIT, accustomed to standing beside other people's endings, are also drawn into the emotional weight of these encounters. Their professional distance begins to waver as they witness how easily love can turn into resentment, silence, dependence, or regret.

The people who come to EXIT gradually learn that ending a relationship does not mean deciding that its happy moments were false. Rather, they must acknowledge both the tenderness that existed and the hurt that now makes separation necessary. Each attempt at goodbye tests whether an honest farewell can be made without denying the past or demanding certainty about the future. By the time the clients step back into their own lives, they have not all found relief, but they have begun to claim responsibility for the endings they had hoped someone else could complete for them.

The musical considers farewell as an act requiring courage, honesty, and care. It asks whether a separation can be sufficient not because it hurts less, but because the people involved finally allow themselves to say what was left unsaid.

show: 크리스마스 캐럴 (Korean title: 「뮤지컬 〈크리스마스 캐럴〉」) — a Korean production, staged at 세종문화회관 M씨어터 in Seoul, 2026
synopsis:
A bitter winter night closes around Scrooge as he dismisses Christmas cheer, scolds his clerk Bob Cratchit for wanting a holiday, and turns away all appeals for generosity. Alone in his house, he is confronted by the ghost of his dead business partner, Marley, who arrives burdened by the consequences of a life spent worshipping money. Marley warns Scrooge that he may yet avoid the same fate, but only if he listens to three spirits who will visit before the night is over.

The first spirit carries Scrooge into his past. He sees the lonely child he once was, separated from warmth and companionship, then the hopeful young man whose love and openness slowly yield to ambition. He witnesses the moment his beloved leaves him, unable to compete with the wealth that has become his only devotion. Next, the spirit of the present reveals a city alive with Christmas fellowship. Scrooge watches his nephew celebrate with friends and enters the modest home of Bob Cratchit, where the family finds joy despite poverty. There he meets Tiny Tim, whose fragile health makes the family's future painfully uncertain.

At last, the spirit of the future shows Scrooge a colder vision: people speak casually of a dead miser, possessions are sold off, and the Cratchit household mourns a child who is gone. Scrooge is led to a neglected grave and recognizes that it bears his own name. Horrified, he begs for another chance. Awakening on Christmas morning, he acts at once: he sends help to the Cratchits, reconciles with his nephew, and begins to live as a generous, attentive member of his community.

The musical centers on the possibility of moral renewal, insisting that no life is beyond change when a person faces the harm they have caused. It celebrates compassion, family, and shared human connection as forces that can transform isolation into hope.

show: 판타지 뮤지컬 오싹한 알바 (Korean title: 「판타지 뮤지컬 〈오싹한 알바〉 - 부산」) — a Korean production, staged at 초콜릿팩토리 in Busan, 2026
synopsis:
A group of struggling theatre actors gathers for another exhausting day, masking private anxieties with rehearsed smiles and banter. When an unusual part-time job appears, it promises a way to keep going, yet its strange conditions draw them into encounters that unsettle the stories they tell about themselves. What first seems like a creepy, comic assignment gradually becomes a space where buried recollections rise to the surface and where each person must face the gap between the cheerful role presented to others and the pain kept hidden within.

As the work continues, the actors discover that the real source of unease is not a conventional ghostly threat but the persistence of unresolved feeling. Their everyday jokes, petty frustrations, ambitions, and disappointments give way to moments of recognition as they listen to one another and confront memories they had tried to leave behind. The job brings their lives into unexpected contact, testing whether they can move beyond performance and speak honestly. Amid songs, rapid comic exchanges, and fantastical turns, their shared experience becomes an opportunity to acknowledge loneliness rather than conceal it. The question is no longer merely how to survive an odd shift, but how to remain present for another person when the past intrudes and ordinary life feels impossible to manage.

The musical treats fear as an emotional condition shaped by memory, isolation, and the effort of pretending to be fine. It ultimately argues for connection: healing begins when people allow themselves to be seen, heard, and remembered.

show: 푸른 꽃 (Korean title: 「뮤지컬 〈푸른 꽃〉」) — produced by ㈜네버엔딩플레이, staged at 충무아트센터 중극장 블랙 in Seoul, 2026
synopsis:
Kreta spends her days on the island where the sun rises first, sharing her fascination with coral with her beloved older friend, Olive. She believes the island’s legend that blue coral can grant a wish, while her mother reads her a book called Blue Flower and her father anxiously watches the sea that will soon swallow their home. When Olive is forced to leave the island, Kreta refuses to accept the separation. Determined to find the miraculous blue coral, she searches more urgently as the adults around her prepare to abandon the place they believe cannot be saved.

Inside the book Kreta reads, a young man named Heinrich travels through a medieval world shaped by merchants, miners, poets, and legends. The people he meets speak to him of poetry and the natural world, opening his imagination to forces larger than himself. One night, Heinrich dreams of a woman appearing within a blue flower. The vision leaves him certain that he is moving toward an encounter that will change his life, and toward a love he has not yet found.

The two narratives echo one another across their distant worlds. Heinrich moves through stories that celebrate the earth and the mysterious connections between people and nature, while Kreta confronts a present in which the sea is rising and the people she loves are preparing to go. As tales, songs, and legends unfold within the wider story, her search for blue coral becomes both a wish to keep Olive close and a desperate appeal to the grown-ups who have decided that surrender is inevitable. Kreta’s voice insists on asking what remains possible when a home, a friendship, and a living world appear to be disappearing.

The musical intertwines longing, love, imagination, and the sustaining force of stories. It contrasts a child’s refusal to give up with an adult world facing environmental loss, asking whether hope can become a form of action.

show: 헤어드레서 (Korean title: 「뮤지컬 〈헤어드레서〉 - 포천」) — produced by (재)예술경영지원센터, staged at 포천반월아트홀 대극장 in Pocheon, 2026
synopsis:
Mare returns from Italy to a Korea poised uneasily between old prohibitions and new possibilities. Gifted with an instinctive eye for colour, form, and personal style, she has long drawn hostile attention for refusing to make herself small; her parents, unable to accept the conspicuous daughter they fear they cannot control, had sent her abroad with a foreign missionary. Now, in the final years of the Joseon era, Mare brings home skills and ideas shaped by a wider world, determined to turn beauty into a vocation rather than a private rebellion.

Her ambition meets a society that regards a woman who works publicly, chooses her own path, and transforms established appearances as a provocation. Mare presses on, using scissors, combs, fabric, and daring imagination to create looks that fuse unfamiliar Western fashions with Korean sensibilities. Each new client and style becomes a declaration that women may be seen on their own terms. Yet visibility brings resistance: public scrutiny grows, conservative expectations close in, and Yehwa, unable to accept Mare's talent and independence, turns envy into open conflict.

As Mare struggles to protect both her work and her sense of self, the world of hairdressing becomes more than ornament. Her designs invite others to imagine changed lives, while the spectacular hair shows surrounding her work turn an intimate craft into a public challenge to the era's rigid rules. Mare must decide whether to retreat into the safety prescribed for her or risk disgrace in pursuit of the future she can already see. Her resolve gradually makes her a figure whose success is inseparable from the courage to remain unmistakably herself.

The musical centres on artistic self-discovery, courage, and a woman's fight for economic and personal independence under social constraint. It treats beauty as a language of freedom: an act of creation capable of confronting prejudice, reshaping identity, and opening space for lives that convention had kept hidden.
